title: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.source_raw: 1.25-1.5 lbs boneless (skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch chunks)
ingredients.notes: Settled line. 156 g raw per serving, in line with the catalog's chicken-breast average.
Settled line.
Settled line.

Corn-salad salt. 6 g/tsp, matching the settled Salt row (1/4 tsp = 1.5 g). REUSE of the live board id `sea-salt` (5 of 7 stores, cheapest 0.1106 at Sam's Club) which names exactly this food; only a vocabulary name row is missing, which is a naming question and not a registrar one. Not bridged onto `salt`, whose price class and grind differ.
Settled line.
Settled line.
Settled line.

ingredients.source_raw: 2 cups cooked corn (I used canned and drained )
ingredients.notes: Drained canned corn at 164 g/cup, the basis the Del Monte can's 3.5 servings against its drained weight gives. The source line itself says 'I used canned and drained', so the vocabulary's Sweet Whole Kernel Corn [canned-corn] is the same food and the 'cooked' form flag is spurious - canned corn is sold cooked. Existing vocabulary id, a reuse.

ingredients.source_raw: ½ cup plain Greek yogurt (I used 2%)
ingredients.notes: 245 g/cup Greek yogurt. Exact vocabulary match (Plain Yogurt and Greek Yogurt both carry [greek-yogurt]), same form. The board's `yogurt` match is regular yogurt, a different price class, so I used the vocabulary's id.

Crumbled cotija at 7 g/tbsp (1/4 cup = 28 g, the existing DB row's basis). Board ABSENT: no commodity and no capture match. Ricotta, provolone and parmesan are different cheeses at different price classes, so no bridge is available; pantry-static pricing on 21 g is safe and the term is reported for pricing.

13.8 g/tbsp. Built with ordinary mayonnaise; the avocado-oil brand is a variant of the same food. Same food and same gram weight; the oil is a brand variant of mayonnaise, not a different product concept, on the sun-dried-tomatoes-oil-packed precedent. Not a new id.
About 30 g juice plus 1 g zest from one lime. Vocabulary row Lime Juice [limes], board MAPPED limes 5 of 7. One whole lime yields about 30 g juice plus 1 g zest, both from the one purchased lime.
14 g per pepper, the USDA per-pepper portion. REUSE of the live board id `jalapenos` (6 of 7, cheapest 1.4277 at Walmart); only the vocabulary name row is missing. Source marks the line optional.

Midpoint of 2-3 tbsp at 1 g/tbsp, the settled cilantro line's own basis. Same food as the settled 'chopped fresh cilantro' line in this recipe; the DIFFERENT FORM flag only reflects the vocabulary name carrying the word 'Fresh', which this line omits.
Settled line.
Tap water for cooking the rice: no commodity and no cost, following the 2026-08-27 'water' ruling. Still weighed at 236.6 g/cup and still printed, because it goes in the pot.
185 g per cup dry long-grain white rice. Exact vocabulary row Rice [rice], same form, board MAPPED 7 of 7. Long-grain is the default white rice, not a form flip.
Rice-cooking salt, 6 g/tsp. Same ruling as the corn-salad sea salt line: reuse of the live `sea-salt` board id, 6 g/tsp.
Settled line.
15 g/tbsp lime juice. Vocabulary row Lime Juice [limes]; 'fresh' is how the vocabulary row is already priced (whole limes squeezed), not a form flip onto a bottled product.
2 g/tsp finely grated zest. Zest comes off the same purchased limes, exactly the Orange Zest -> citrus-fruit precedent the vocabulary already uses. Source marks the line 'or to taste'.
Settled line.

ingredients.source_raw: Pickled red onions or fresh red onions (chopped)
ingredients.notes: Source never quantified this topping; 30 g at source scale is about a quarter of a small red onion per 4 servings. Standing rejection: red onion is not `onions` (variety pricing), so the board's 7 of 7 onions match cannot carry it. Unquantified topping weighed at 30 g source scale; term reported for pricing.
Settled line.

Unquantified garnish sprinkle, weighed at about 1 tbsp per serving at source scale. Same ruling as the corn-salad cotija line: board ABSENT, no same-concept id exists, pantry-static pricing on a 15 g garnish is safe.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 553 cal / 57 carbs / 45 protein per serving over 4 servings. Recomputed at source scale from the DB rows above plus the settled rows: 2476 cal, 181.3 g protein, 232.6 g carbs, 92 g fat total, i.e. 619 cal / 45.3 P / 58.2 C per serving. PROTEIN AGREES TO +0.7% (45.3 vs 45) and carbs to +2%, both far inside the 15% bar, which confirms the 623.7 g chicken basis (156 g raw per serving, against the catalog's 167 g average) and the 185 g dry rice basis. Calories run +12% high, and the reason is legible: the source's panel almost certainly excludes the three assembly toppings it never quantified (avocado 240 cal, garnish cotija 48, red onion 13). Drop those and the recipe recomputes to 544 cal per serving against the published 553, a -1.6% gap. Against this run's enforced band, the full dish is 619 cal (450-800 ok) and 45.3 g protein (>= 40 ok), with boneless skinless chicken breast as the main protein and rice as the real carbohydrate.
